text:
Jordan: heads up — ran the 8-node TP scaling job (master branch + recent batcher change) and we hit a sharp throughput collapse around step 120. several ranks show long allgather tails and one rank timed out. attaching the short log snippet i captured. :eyes:

Maya: can you paste the batcher config you used? also which kernel selector flags?

Jordan: config below:
```
batcher:
  strategy: slab
  slab_size_tokens: 512
  max_batch_tokens: 32768
  allow_cross_host_pack: true
kernel_selector:
  prefer_shared_kernels: false
  quant_fallback: auto
```
kernel selector was default on main.

Sasha: quick note from nsys on one failed run — GPU 2 shows repeated long launches of `allreduce_async` (avg 160ms) while others are ~10-20ms. looks like comm backpressure + one rank doing heavier compute kernels. got a small flamegraph.

Liam: slab packing with slab_size 512 can create microbatch imbalance if token distribution is skewed. some ranks end up packing larger microbatches and trigger different kernel paths (e.g., the large-matmul kernel with less optimized shared memory).

Jordan: log snippet:
```
[2102345678.12] Rank 4 WARN: allgather tail 0.162s (expected <0.02s)
[2102345678.13] Rank 4 ERROR: rendezvous timeout waiting for allgather from rank 2
[2102345678.13] Rank 2 INFO: kernel chosen=matmul_large_shared, time=0.148s
[2102345678.14] Rank 6 INFO: kernel chosen=matmul_fast, time=0.018s
```

Olivia: any NVLINK errors or PCIe retries in dmesg? sometimes hw transport hiccups amplify software imbalance.

Jordan: checked dmesg on nodes, nothing obvious. NCCL logs show some retries on rank 2 during the window.

Maya: can you run with slab_size_tokens=128 and with `kernel_selector.prefer_shared_kernels=true` to force the smaller kernel path? also flip `allow_cross_host_pack=false` to avoid cross-host packing for a test.

Jordan: running that now on a small repro subset (4 nodes, same batch distribution). starting trace with infra-bot (nsys).

infra-bot: created trace job 2102345678-comm-trace, link: https://internal.traces/2102345678/comm-trace

Sasha: looking at the nsys timeline — when cross-host pack is on, there's a window where one host packs 2 extra microbatches into a slab because of token rounding. that host then selects `matmul_large_shared` which is ~8x slower for the microshape we have. while it's stuck, other ranks pile up NCCL ops and the allreduce experiences head-of-line blocking.

Liam: that explains it. suggestion: batcher should prefer balanced token distribution across hosts and implement a max-slab-delta guard so no host can exceed the median slab by more than 1 slab_size. also consider preferring kernel paths by measured flops/latency for the exact microshape instead of coarse thresholds.

Maya: small quick patch idea: when building slabs, compute per-host token_estimate and if max-min > slab_size_tokens then trim the largest host pack. low-risk and easy to A/B.

Jordan: applied the trimming patch locally and reran — preliminary result: no long allgather tails in 3/3 short runs. throughput stable. will run full 8-node in 10m.

Olivia: :thumbsup: good. we should also add a metric in Console: slab_skew_count and kernel_path_mismatch_rate so we can alert when skew > threshold.

Sasha: opened a small profiling PR with a helper to log "chosen_kernel" and microshape per rank to S3 for 100 steps. will attach along with the trace.

Liam: one more note — rendezvous should tolerate transient kernel-driven stalls by allowing a slightly larger per-op slack on allgather before hard timeout, and surface a warning rather than immediate failure for 1 retry. avoids noisy incidents for small skew.

Jordan: full 8-node run finished with the trimming change: steady state maintained, no timeouts. saving traces to s3://perf-debug/2102345678. I'll open a PR with the batcher trim + tests.

Maya: action items:
- Jordan: open PR with trimming patch + repro script (assigned)
- Sasha: add kernel/microshape logging to profiler (assigned)
- Liam: prototype slab_skew detector in rendezvous and a soft-timeout fallback (assigned)
- Olivia: add Console metric proposal for slab skew and kernel mismatch (follow-up)

Jordan: thanks all. will link PR + traces in this thread when ready. :rocket:
